wine_name: Howard Park Leston Shiraz, Margaret River
wrong_facts: Hook claims Leston vineyard sits on 'ironstone ridge' - the ground truth says Leston Vineyard is in Wilyabrup; ironstone ridge is not verified
Hook implies Leston is a place/vineyard name tied to geography - ground truth says Leston is a family name (Jeff Burch's father)
Vinification says 'destemmed but not crushed, allowing a portion of whole berries to ferment carbonically' - ground truth says 10% whole bunch fermentation (whole bunch ≠ whole berry/carbonic)
Claims 'wild-yeast fermentation peaks at 30°C for eight days' - not in context data and unverifiable
Claims 'still 4 g/L residual sugar' at pressing - fabricated number
Claims '6 tonnes/ha, half the regional average' - fabricated yield number
Claims 'afternoon sea breezes that drop temperatures 8°C before sunset' - fabricated specific number
Claims '180 m elevation' for the ridge - unverifiable/likely fabricated
Claims 'A$38-45 locally, US$32-38 import markets' - no price data provided and unverifiable
Oak regime described as '30% new French oak' matches ground truth but omits the 5% American oak component; also the whole-bunch detail is wrong (says whole berry not whole bunch)
reasoning: The output is extremely well-written with outstanding voice and specificity, but it fabricates numerous specific numbers (yield, fermentation temp, residual sugar, elevation, prices, temperature drop) none of which appear in the context data. The hook implies Leston is a geographic/vineyard ridge name when ground truth confirms it's a family name (Jeff Burch's father). The vinification section gets the whole-bunch detail wrong (says whole berry carbonic maceration vs. 10% whole bunch fermentation). The 18 months/30% new French oak detail matches ground truth, which is good. But the sheer volume of fabricated specifics — while making the output read convincingly — is exactly the kind of confident-sounding AI slop that damages trust. The hard penalty for fabricated numbers should apply, but there are so many fabricated numbers across multiple fields that this is a systemic issue rather than a single slip.
